title: Warp Terminal Pricing: Plans and Credit Costs (2026)
summary: Warp terminal pricing spans free and commercial tiers with different capabilities and usage limits. Identify the plan that suits your needs.
body_markdown:
## Running Warp Agent Jobs on a Schedule With Activepieces


If the bundled estimate holds, you still have one gap: Warp is built for you sitting at the terminal, and a job that must run every night or fire on an event belongs in a workflow tool.


Activepieces bills a flow run as 1 credit however many steps it has, where Zapier charges per task, so splitting a ten-step job into smaller, safer steps costs the same as the two-step version.


### What fits a workflow tool and what stays in the terminal


A nightly summary of what changed in a repository, a review kicked off when a pull request opens, a docs check every Monday: if you'd otherwise remember to do it by hand on a clock or a trigger, it's a workflow job.


Skip the workflow tool for these and the cost is a task that depends on someone remembering, which means it eventually doesn't happen.


When you steer, read the output and decide the next step, the work stays in Warp. That's the work your Warp credit allowance is meant to cover, so keep it there.


Because Activepieces connects 747 integrations and runs steps on a schedule or a trigger, it doesn't replace Warp; it can sit in front of the work you already do. It adds a second meter to your bill, and that's the one to price.


### How job execution costs in credits


Run an unattended job on[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) and it draws from its own monthly credits, separate from Warp's.


A plain run is 1 credit, and an AI step inside it costs 2 credits on a fast model, 10 on a smart one and 20 on a frontier one.


The table below shows the three plans as listed on[activepieces.com/pricing](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) at the time of writing, so current prices may have changed since publication.


Read the last column as a rough fit, and expect to adjust it once you count how many steps each of your jobs runs.


Plan Monthly price Credits Suited to


Free $0 1,000 One or two light jobs you are testing before you rely on them


Plus $20 10,000 A handful of recurring jobs that run daily


Team $200 50,000 Many jobs, or event-triggered ones that fire unpredictably


Nothing is charged on the Free row, so it's where you learn how fast a real job uses credits. The Plus row gives ten times the credits for a modest monthly fee.


The Team row only pays off if event-triggered jobs would otherwise run you out of credits mid-month.


So run one job for a week on Free, count what it used, and multiply by your job list before you pick a plan.
